land.text: the land of Jersika, a tributary of Polotsk (infobox 'Preceded by: Principality of Polotsk')

predecessors.note: The Polotsk page names Jersika among the smaller fiefs and says it 'had previously been under the control of Polotsk' (1209); the Polotsk dossier carries a 1101 split event.

land.text: Visvaldis's fief (Jersika, Mākoņkalns and Naujiene), which 'passed to the Livonian Order' after his death in 1239

successors.note: The Livonian Order is the Teutonic Order's Livonian branch; the Livonian Brothers of the Sword dossier ends in 1237. The part of Jersika controlled by Albert (Lettia) was divided in 1211 between the bishopric of Riga and the Brothers of the Sword (see archbishopric-of-riga and livonian-brothers-of-the-sword).

capitals.name: Jersika
capitals.note: The hill fort stood on the right bank of the Daugava in Līvāni Municipality, about 165 km southeast of Riga (Jersika village page). No page opened gives coordinates and the gazetteer has no entry; the point is the centroid of Cliopatria's 1111 shape, to be replaced once 'Jersika' is added to the gazetteer.

keyframe_review.note: 23,422 km2 for 1111-1205. The page gives no area (infobox 'Area: not given') and a disputed origin: 'the Principality of Jersika had emerged in 1041' (a saga, 'only a suggestion'), infobox 'Established: 1041/1190', existence in the 12th century 'more certain', first mention 1203. The shape stands from 1111 at confidence 1; nothing on the page dates its frontier.
23,278 km2 for 1206-1209, 145 km2 less than the 1111 shape; a grid-level change that no event on the page explains. Kept.

13,850 km2 for 1210-1215. In 1209 Visvaldis 'lost the lands of Autīne and Cesvaine, but retained Jersika, Mākoņkalns and Naujiene' and received the rest of his realm back from Albert 'as a fief'; the 1206-to-1210 reduction (11,900 km2, all in the west) is that loss. The shape is the retained fief.

correction.text: the 1210 shape carried forward: Visvaldis's fief, held until his death in 1239

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, confidence 1: Cliopatria's Jersika row ends in 1215, but the page says 'After the death of Visvaldis in 1239, his fief passed to the Livonian Order' (infobox 'Disestablished: 1239'). The page does not say how far the fief reached after the 1211 division and the 1214 sack, so the 1210 shape is bridged.

ledger.note: 1111: Cliopatria opens the Jersika row; the page does not date the founding. The saga date 1041 is 'only a suggestion', the infobox gives 'Established: 1041/1190', the principality's existence in the 12th century is 'more certain' and its ruler Visvaldis is 'first mentioned in 1203'. The row's start is kept as a bridging judgment.

region.text: the lands of Autīne and Cesvaine and the part of the realm Albert did not return as a fief

ledger.note: 1209: Albert of Riga defeats Visvaldis of Jersika, who loses Autīne and Cesvaine and holds the rest as Riga's fief. 'In 1209, Visvaldis, the prince of Jersika, was defeated by the bishop Albert of Riga'; 'He lost the lands of Autīne and Cesvaine, but retained Jersika, Mākoņkalns and Naujiene'; 'He was forced to submit his kingdom to Albert as a grant to the Bishopric of Riga' and received part back as a fief. The region is the part of Cliopatria's 1206 shape missing from its 1210 shape.

region.text: Visvaldis's fief, Jersika, Mākoņkalns and Naujiene

ledger.note: 1239: Visvaldis dies and his fief passes to the Livonian Order. 'After the death of Visvaldis in 1239, his fief passed to the Livonian Order' (repeatedly contested by the rulers of Lithuania and Novgorod).
The Principality of Jersika ends with Visvaldis's death; infobox 'Disestablished: 1239'.

wars.name: Livonian conquest of Jersika

zones.text: Autīne, Cesvaine and the realm not returned as a fief

wars.outcome: Albert of Riga defeated Visvaldis in 1209, who lost Autīne and Cesvaine and held the rest as a fief of the bishopric; in 1211 'the part of Jersika controlled by Albert' was divided between the bishopric and the Brothers of the Sword; in 1212 Polotsk gave up its tributary rights over Jersika in Albert's favour; in 1214 'Germans attacked the Castle of Jersika and sacked it'.
wars.note: Polotsk's page (1209, 1212) gives the same conquest from the Polotsk side: 'German crusaders conquered the principalities of Jersika and Koknese ... which had previously been under the control of Polotsk', forcing Polotsk 'to permit free travel to German merchants in 1212 and ending Livonian tributes'.

certainty.note: A hill-fort lordship on the Daugava; the pages name castles and districts (Jersika, Mākoņkalns, Naujiene, Autīne, Cesvaine), never a frontier line.

sources.title: Principality of Jersika
sources.note: Identity, origin dispute, 1209 defeat and fief, 1211 division, 1212, 1214, 1239; read twice (second time for the exact paragraph on 1209-1239).

sources.title: Principality of Polotsk
sources.note: Jersika and Koknese among the smaller fiefs; 1209 conquest, 1212 treaty.

sources.title: Jersika
sources.note: Village page opened for coordinates: gives none; the hill fort lies on the Daugava in Līvāni Municipality, 165 km southeast of Riga.

notes: Pages opened: 3 for a budget of 1-2 (the third, the Jersika village page, was opened only to find the capital's coordinates and gave none). Infobox area: none. START: Cliopatria opens in 1111; the page offers 1041 (a saga, 'only a suggestion') and the infobox '1041/1190', with first mention in 1203; the found event keeps 1111 at confidence 1. END: Cliopatria ends in 1215, the page keeps Visvaldis's fief until his death in 1239, so the dossier ends in 1239 and bridges 1216-1239 at confidence 1; the Livonian Brothers of the Sword dossier has a gain from principality-of-jersika in 1210 (confidence 1) that covers the lost western part only if read from the 1211 division; this dossier gives the 1209 loss to the Bishopric of Riga (archbishopric-of-riga) and the 1211 division is the Riga and Sword Brothers dossiers' to carry. Not settled: the vassal relation (Visvaldis's fief of Riga from 1209; Polotsk's tribute to 1212) belongs to the Riga dossier as a vassal_start for principality-of-jersika; the capital's coordinates; the area of the retained fief (Cliopatria's 13.8 k km2 is a reading). Gazetteer: 'Jersika', 'Autīne' and 'Mākoņkalns' are not gazetteer places.
